verdict.label: RED · Stand down / roll DTE longer — AI/chip selloff in its sixth session, VIX above 30, and a breakout board that is fighting a falling tape
verdict.desc: The rout keeps going. Thursday the S&P 500 fell 2.02% to 7,175.83, its sixth straight decline, and overnight the AI/chip complex sold off again across Asia and Europe — S&P futures are down ~0.7% and Nasdaq-100 futures ~1.5% pre-open, with Anthropic giving back more than 7% after its debut pop. The VIX pushed above 30 intraday, an ~8-month high, the 10-year holds around 5.05%, and gold and oil are both sliding. Composite gap-risk sits at 72 (HOT) and P(≥1% gap) is ~50%, well above the 35% trigger, so GREEN is locked out. The scanner boarded two Type C names — DIS (Grade A, a breakout that has held one session) and SH (Grade B+, the inverse-S&P ETF breaking out on the selloff) — but selling bull-put premium into a VIX-above-30, sixth-down-day tape is exactly what 4-VAL exists to prevent. Honor the board as watch-only; sell nothing new today and re-run tomorrow.

focus.jtag: The AI/chip rout deepened again: Thursday the S&P fell 2.02% to 7,175.83 for a sixth straight loss, overnight tech dropped across Asia and Europe, and futures point lower with Anthropic reversing its debut pop. The VIX is above 30 and the 10-year sits near 5%. The scanner boarded two Type C breakouts — DIS, a held ATH breakout, and SH, the inverse-S&P ETF breaking out on the very selloff that makes the tape dangerous
focus.jnote: The scanner boarded two breakouts, but the tape is a sixth-day AI/chip rout with the VIX above 30 — that contradiction is the signal. On Thursday the S&P 500 ended 2.02% lower at 7,175.83, down 147.80 points, while the Nasdaq Composite fell 2.25% to 23,879.2 and the Dow lost 2.19% to 49,097.06. Overnight the selling continued: tech stocks fell in Asia and Europe after Thursday's selling on Wall Street. Pre-open Nasdaq 100 futures were down 1.6% and S&P 500 futures 0.7% at about 7 a.m. Eastern, while Dow futures were flat, and Anthropic pulled back more than 6% in pre-market after closing up about 17% on its debut. The fear gauge is stretched: the VIX surged past 30 to its highest level in nearly eight months, hitting its intraday high since late March. A Sniper does not sell premium into that.
focus.notdown: DIS (Walt Disney) is the scanner's cleanest boarded name — a Type C ATH breakout that has held one session above its $119.65 pivot on ~2x volume, with the 52-week high at $123.37. The structure is real: the stock printed a 52-week range top of 123.37 and multiple brokers raised targets after the fiscal Q4 report. But honesty the board requires: the overnight quote is soft — DIS closed at $120.25 on 11/19 and was indicated ~+0.5% pre-market around $120.86, barely above the pivot into a risk-off open. A breakout bull-put needs a calm, bid tape; today isn't it. Watch-only.
focus.notup: SH (ProShares Short S&P500) is the second boarded name, tagged bullish — and the honest tension is that it is an inverse ETF, so a Type C bull-put on SH is a bet the S&P keeps falling. It is “breaking out” only because the market is selling off: SH opened at $34.68 Friday, up ~2.0%, with a fifty-day average of $32.57 and a 52-week high of $39.20. The scanner flags two hard gates — no open-interest data returned and no next-earnings date (both expected for an ETF). Selling premium on a leveraged-to-the-selloff instrument while the VIX is above 30 is a squeeze-on-any-bounce trap. Sell nothing new today.
focus.why: Why RED? Three things stack. One: composite 72 is HOT and P(≥1% gap) at ~50% is well above the 35% trigger — either alone locks out GREEN. Two: the VIX pushed above 30, an ~8-month high, into a sixth straight S&P loss and a deepening AI/chip rout, with the 10-year near 5% — a stretched, two-sided tape where any bounce squeezes hard. Three: the two boarded names, while honored on the board, are a breakout barely holding its pivot into a gap-down (DIS) and an inverse-ETF “breakout” that is really a bet the selloff continues (SH) — neither is the calm, bid setup a bull-put breakout needs. Stand down on new credit spreads, treat the board as watch-only, and re-run tomorrow. Cash is a position today.

risks: AI/chip rout in its sixth session — the S&P fell for a sixth straight day as the tech sell-off continues to astound, and AMD, Taiwan Semiconductor, Micron, Intel and Nvidia were all lower pre-market. A failed bounce is the base-case risk and the core reason the verdict is RED.

VIX above 30 — the fear gauge surged past 30 to its highest level in nearly eight months, its intraday high since late March. Elevated vol fattens the overnight gap tail in both directions — any relief bounce squeezes bearish positioning violently.

10-year near 5% & a hawkish Fed — the 10-year Treasury yield was around 5.06% into a hawkish outlook ahead of the Dec 9 decision. A rate backdrop this tight caps any oversold bounce and keeps pressure on high-multiple tech.

SH setup is an inverse-ETF ‘breakout’ — the second boarded name profits only if the S&P keeps falling, and SH opened at $34.68, up ~2.0%, purely on the selloff. Its OI and next-earnings fields came back blank — verify before treating it as anything but watch-only.

Oil, gold & broad de-risking — WTI declined ~1.95% to $81.59 as Middle East export flows recovered, while gold fell ~2.3% to around $3,543. Simultaneous weakness across equities, crude and gold signals indiscriminate de-risking, not a clean rotation.
